title: Building Cirrus: a single-user, serverless PDS

I'm here to talk about Sirus, which is my PDS. So, I I have built a PDS that I use to help self-host, and I hopefully might convince some of you people here to self-host your PDS as well. But first, what is a PDS? PDS is a Personal Data Server. It is where all of your stuff is. On the App Proto Network. Now, a lot of people here probably know this, but your PDS holds pretty much everything on the App Proto Network for you. It's all of your posts, of course, but it's also all of your likes and your friends and your whole social graph. But it's also everything from any of your other third-party apps that you're working with. All of the different network, all of the things on the app protein network live on your PDS. They also, all of the blobs live on there as well, which are the files, the images, and the videos, and things like that. So the whole point of a PDS is to make it so that you are able to have the network as decentralized so that you own all of your data. And what I didn't realize is, as well as being where all your data is, it's also where you talk to. So it's where your API calls go when you're using the network. So when you've got the, like, Bluesky app, for example, on your phone or on the web, it's not talking to Bluesky when it's connected. If you look at the network panel, and honestly, I mean, the first time I knew this was when I opened up the network panel and saw that it was hitting my PDS. You talk directly to your PDS. So all of your connections and everything go directly to your PDS. So most of the stuff a PDS does is talking to you. This, obviously, your PDS doesn't have all of the data on it. Most of the data on the network is somewhere else. So for anything that it doesn't have, like all of your timeline and everything else, it proxies it to the app view, which, you know, in most cases is Blue Sky, which holds everything. But how does the— how does Blue Sky or the rest of the network get your data? It's done through a relay. So there are two relays that BlueSky has, US East and US West. They recently changed them around. And basically, your PDS, when you publish something, it sends it out to the relay. So the way that works is it's a WebSocket, like a permanent WebSocket. The relay connects to your WebSocket, and whenever you post something, it sends it out into your— into the relay. And as you can probably see from this at the moment, it's not actually doing a huge amount of work, the PDS, per person. It's only doing something when you post on it or when you make a query on it because the app view isn't— so when somebody goes and looks at your timeline, they aren't hitting your PDS. What they're doing is it's being relayed to the app view from the relays. And the relays hold every single, every single post on the network. Every single record, every single event on the network goes through the relays, and they send it off to the app view. So, all of the work, really, the heavy work is done by the relays and the app view. So, it's a PDS, doesn't actually do a huge amount of work, Anyone can host them, but that's not what people are doing. So, you know, 99 point— I mean, these are numbers as of last week. 99.4% of all users are using the Blue Sky PDSs. They're the mushroom ones. They're named after mushrooms.
